patterns.what_worked: Kusto GetDefaultDenyViolationDetails query surfaced zero violating endpoints quickly, confirming the pipeline was already network-isolation clean. Applying DefaultDeny (removing Permissive, keeping CFSClean/CFSClean2/CFSClean3) was a one-line YAML change in the OneBranch featureFlags.networkisolation.policy parameter. Branch validation via a real pipeline run plus deep log inspection (Start/Stop Network Isolation task logs) gave concrete, verifiable proof (zero blocked connections, all four policies COMPLIANT) rather than relying on inference.
patterns.what_was_hard: The build surfaced an unrelated EACCES failure during a later test task (extension install via run-integration-tests.mjs), which required a lengthy separate investigation to definitively rule out as network-isolation-caused versus a CI infra flake. The ADO pipeline_build_log MCP tool was unreliable (repeated remote connection errors) requiring a fallback to raw REST API calls with manual log-id-to-task-name mapping, which was tedious.
patterns.improvisation: Used the 'Stop Network Isolation' task log's explicit 'Blocked connections' and 'Policy violations: ... Status = [ COMPLIANT ]' output as definitive proof of compliance, rather than only the resolution-criteria (7-day/3-run) dashboard mentioned in the skill's Step 4 — this gave an immediate, high-confidence signal without waiting on the multi-day criterion.
patterns.recurring_pattern: The MCP pipeline log tool intermittently fails with remote connection errors on some ADO orgs/projects, forcing a raw REST + curl fallback; seen before in this same investigation for multiple individual log ids.
patterns.tsg_gap: The skill's Step 4 doesn't mention that the per-run 'Stop Network Isolation' task log already reports per-policy COMPLIANT/violation status immediately after a single run, which is a much faster confidence signal than waiting for the 7-day/3-run dashboard criterion. Adding this as an intermediate validation tip would help future sessions.
patterns.environment_blockers: ado-pipelines_build_log MCP tool intermittently failed with 'Remote connection error: Remote connection error after 4 attempts' on several log ids for this build, requiring a raw curl+REST API workaround.

outcome.changes_proposed: Remove Permissive, apply DefaultDeny (with CFSClean,CFSClean2,CFSClean3 preserved) to microsoft/vscode-cosmosdb's .azure-pipelines/build.yml (OneBranch template), deprecating 1esmain.yml as a duplicate/inactive pipeline definition.
outcome.full_journey: Fetched S360 KPI metadata and the specific action item (target 188bc6f1-...) for ES-4.2.4 (SFI, DefaultDeny). [user] clarified 1esmain.yml was deprecated and only build.yml was active, narrowing scope to a single OneBranch pipeline. Ran GetDefaultDenyViolationDetails Kusto query (re-run once on request) confirming zero violating endpoints. Drafted a netiso exception request per user request, then discussed which unrelated cases (from telemetry) were unrelated to Electron tests, and reviewed pipeline logs together with [user] before producing an updated exception draft. Created branch dev/sevoku/es424-defaultdeny off latest main, committed the build.yml DefaultDeny change (Permissive removed, CFSClean/CFSClean2/CFSClean3 + DefaultDeny applied), opened a draft PR, and manually triggered a pipeline run for validation. [user] supplied security contacts (adrianmi@microsoft.com, simonec@microsoft.com) and team alias (vscode-cosmosdb@microsoft.com) for use in the exception/PR context. Checked build status multiple times; when [user] asked whether the change had taken effect, confirmed via the 'Start Network Isolation' log that DefaultDeny/CFSClean* were indeed the active policies for that run (change had taken effect). [user] chose to leave the PR as-is rather than retry the pipeline.
